citation: Wang X, Qin X-M, Ji S, Dong D (2023). Effects of Resistance Training with Blood Flow Restriction on Explosive Power of Lower Limbs: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. Journal of Human Kinetics.
population: Healthy individuals aged 13–34 years, predominantly young adult athletes and physically active adults; both sexes included.
intervention: Blood flow restriction training (BFRT) at 20–35% 1RM with cuff occlusion at proximal thigh (cuff width ≥10 cm, pressure individualized to arterial occlusion pressure) during exercise, 2–4 resistance exercises per session, 2–3 sessions/week for 3–4 weeks, compared to traditional resistance training (TRT).
summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 12 controlled trials (262 participants) found that blood flow restriction training (BFRT) produced significantly greater improvements in lower-limb explosive power than traditional resistance training (TRT). BFRT showed small-to-moderate benefits for jump (SMD 0.36), sprint (SMD 0.54), and power (SMD 0.54) performance, with wide cuffs (≥10 cm) applied during exercise yielding the largest effects.
key_findings: Jump performance improved more with BFRT than TRT: SMD = 0.36 (95% CI 0.02 to 0.69), p < 0.05, based on 8 studies.
Sprint performance improved more with BFRT than TRT: SMD = 0.54 (95% CI 0.00 to 1.07), p = 0.05, based on 6 studies.
Power performance improved more with BFRT than TRT: SMD = 0.54 (95% CI 0.17 to 1.27), p = 0.01, based on 5 studies.
BFRT with wide cuffs (≥10 cm) during training produced greater explosive power gains than narrow cuffs or restriction only during rest intervals.
Training periods as short as 8 days to 3–4 weeks elicited significant improvements in explosive power with BFRT.
limitations: Only 12 studies (262 participants) were included, with moderate methodological quality (PEDro median 5/10). The small number of trials limits the precision of pooled estimates and precludes robust subgroup analyses.
